fields.name: BatchExtensions Add overload family
fields.contract: BatchExtensions exposes one Add extension family for composing a Batch from a Query contract. A ShardBatch<TResult> or DatabaseBatch<TResult> receiver selects the result shape: a comparable scalar record, a sequence of records, a virtual compound key or key sequence with optional child identity and optional shard-identifier column, or a model produced by a supplied QueryResultModelHandler. Every overload whose receiver type uses the receiver's own generically-typed Add(BatchStep<TResult>) adds one matching result operation and returns the original receiver; the List<TRecord> and List<ShardKey<...>> receiver overloads do not reach that outcome (see asymmetry 3). Overloads either accept an explicit DbParameterCollection or use an empty parameter collection; record and key type arguments are comparable, and model type arguments have a public parameterless constructor. Three asymmetries hold within the family: (1) when a model step needs no caller-supplied argument, the overload still constructs its step with all four arguments, supplying a QueryResultModelHandler<object,TModel> and passing null as the argument rather than omitting it; (2) among the data-column overloads, the IList<TRecord> and List<TRecord> list-result forms exist only with an explicit DbParameterCollection, while the TRecord scalar form offers both a parameterized overload and a parameterless overload that supplies an empty parameter collection; (3) the key-sequence result shape is duplicated across two distinct collection types — for every combination of key arity (ShardKey<TRecord> or ShardKey<TRecord,TChild>), parameter presence, and shard-identifier-column presence, a full, separately-declared overload exists for both an IList<ShardKey<...>> receiver and a List<ShardKey<...>> receiver, and the plain data-column family likewise duplicates its IList<TRecord> overload with a List<TRecord> receiver; every List<>-receiver overload in this family adds its step by casting the receiver to the non-generic System.Collections.IList rather than calling the receiver's own generically-typed Add. That cast does not succeed for any receiver this family can actually be called on: BatchBase<TResult> implements only ICollection and IEnumerable<BatchStep<TResult>>, and neither ShardBatch<TResult> nor DatabaseBatch<TResult> adds an IList implementation of its own, so no instance of either type satisfies IList. Calling any List<>-receiver overload therefore fails that cast before the step is registered, instead of adding the step and returning the receiver the way every other overload in the family does.

sources.label: ShardKey list family duplicated across IList<> and List<> receivers; List<> forms add via an explicit (IList) cast
Plain data-column List<TRecord> overloads also add via an explicit (IList) cast
BatchBase<TResult> implements only ICollection and IEnumerable<BatchStep<TResult>>, not IList
ShardBatch<TResult> derives from BatchBase<TResult> and adds no IList implementation
DatabaseBatch<TResult> derives from BatchBase<TResult> and adds no IList implementation
